# Bedikat Chametz (Spanish)

Source: Halachipedia: Bedikat Chametz (Spanish)

Link: [https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Bedikat_Chametz_%28Spanish%29](https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Bedikat_Chametz_%28Spanish%29)

Exported: 2025-12-30

# Bedikat Chametz
## Texto para Bedikat Chametz
### **Brakha**
1. Antes de la Bedikah, debe hacerse la Brakha de “Al Biur Chametz”(1). Si por accidente se dijo la Brakha de “Al Bitul Chametz”, se cumple con la obligación BeDiavad(2). También se cumple con la obligación si se dijo “LeVaer Chametz”(3).

2.           No se debe hablar entre la Brakha y el inicio de la Bedikah, y si se hizo una interrupción hablando cualquier tema que no tenga relación con la Bedikah, debe repetirse la bendición(4).

3.           Una vez que se ha iniciado, es preferible no hablar sino hasta después de que se haya concluido la Bedikah, sin embargo está permitido hablar inclusive de temas que no estén relacionados a la Bedikah(5).

4.           Si no se hizo la Brakha antes de iniciar la Bedikah, puede recitarse siempre y cuando no se haya terminado la Bedikah. No obstante, si ya termino la Bedikah, deberá recitarse sin Shem UMalkhut en la mañana antes de quemar el Chametz, y hay quienes dicen que puede decirse con Shem UMalkhut(6).

5.           Se puede recitar la Brakhah por la Bedikah delante de muchas personas, las cuales luego se separaran para inspeccionar cada una un área del recinto(7). Si uno de estos no escucho la Brakhah y es imposible terminar la Bedikah sin la participación de esa persona, podrá terminar sin decir la Brakha de nuevo(8).

6.           Si tiene la intención de inspeccionar más de un recinto, es suficiente con una sola Brakha para inspeccionarlos(9).

7.           No recitamos SheHeCheianu por la Bedikah(10).

8.           Hay quienes dicen que se debe hacer Netilat Iadaim antes de hacer la Bedikah(11).

### **Bitul**
1. Después de la Bedikah debe recitarse la siguiente frase de Bitul Chametz:

“כל חמירא וחמיעא דאיכא ברשותי, דלא חזיתיה ודלא בערתיה, לבטיל ולהוי הפקר כעפרא דארעא”

Lo que quiere decir “Todo Chametz, leudo o fermento que se halle en mi posesión, que no haya visto o destruido, será anulado y se considerará sin dueño y será como el polvo de la tierra”(12). Para más información ver la página de Bitul Chametz.

## ¿Cuando?
1. La Bedikat Chametz debe llevarse a cabo al inicio de la noche del catorce de Nisan(13).

2.        Si vamos de acuerdo a la opinion de רבינו תם, hay quienes dicen que debe hacerse después de Tzeit HaKochavim de(14) רבינו תם, y hay quienes dicen que debe empezarse antes de Tzeit HaKochavim de רבינו תם en el momento aceptado de Tzeit HaKochavim (mientras aun hay algo de luz en el horizonte)(15).

3.        Si se reza con un Minian, primero debe concluir su plegaria y después llevar a cabo la Bedikah. Sin embargo, si se reza en casa, se puede designar a alguien para que haga la Bedikah mientras uno reza, de otro modo debe rezar primero. No obstante, quien reza siempre en su casa podría realizar la Bedikah primero de acuerdo a ciertas opiniones. La opinión mayoritaria es que debe rezar primero en cualquier circunstancia(16). Hay quienes recomiendan que la persona que reza en casa debe rezar Maariv en su tiempo, que es Tzeit HaKochavim, y luego empezar la Bedikah(17).

4.        Si se tiene certeza de que va a llegar a casa después de Tzeit HaKochavim, puede designar un agente (Shliach) para que se haga en su tiempo apropiado. Sin embargo, si el hombre labora de noche y quiere llevar a cabo la Mitzvah el mismo, puede designar a su esposa para que haga la Bedikah (sin Brakhah) en toda la casa dejando solo un dormitorio sin inspeccionar, luego hace la Bedikah (con Brakhah) en ese aposento cuando regrese(18).

## ¿Qué?
1. Algunos Poskim dicen que hay que buscar hasta la migaja de Chametz más pequeña y deshacerse de ella (19). Sin embargo, la mayoría de Poskim dicen que no hay obligación de buscar migajas de Chametz sino en los lugares en los que se tendrá comida Kosher para Pesach, los cuales deben ser limpiados meticulosamente para que ni siquiera una migaja de Chametz entre en contacto con la comida destinada para Pesach(20).

2.        El Chametz que se halla en las hendiduras del piso o en la parte de atrás entre un mueble y un muro al que no se puede llegar con facilidad no aplica para la Bedikah(21).

## Limpiar la Casa de Antemano
1. Hay que limpiar o aspirar la casa antes de llevar a cabo la Bedikah(22)

2.        La costumbre es limpiar la casa bien y quitar todo el Chametz de la casa antes de la Bedikah y luego realizar una inspección superficial de la casa sin revisar grietas y hendiduras(23). Lo mismo aplica si la casa fue limpiada y aseada por un no Judio.(24).

3.        En los aposentos en los que se come Chametz se debe revisar bajo las camas y demás muebles, sin embargo, en los aposentos en los que no se come Chametz es suficiente barrer debajo de las camas y gabinetes sin que la inspección sea exhaustiva(25.

## ¿Quién?
1. Alguien que se halle enfermo debe designar un שליח para que haga la Bedikah en su lugar(26).

2.        Alguien que se halle en estado de Onen, es decir, que está en su primer día de duelo, debe designar un שליח para que haga la Bedikah en su lugar(27).

## Marchándose para Pesach
1. Si la persona se marcha de su hogar más de treinta días antes de Pesach y no planea regresar sino hasta después de Pesach, no necesita hacer la Bedikah en ese lugar, sino simplemente hace un Bitul en donde se encuentre cuando llegue el momento en que se hace la Bedikah normalmente (28).

2.        Si la persona se marcha de su casa dentro de los treinta días antes de Pesach y no planea regresar para Pesach, debe hacer la Bedikah con una vela la noche antes de marcharse y hacer Bitul Chametz después, no obstante esta Bedikah se hace sin Brakha(29).

a.        Debido a que la persona no va a estar en su casa para Pesach, es suficiente con hacer una Bedikah apropiada de acuerdo a la Ley simplemente buscando Chametz (aunque no debe ser superficial solamente) y no hay que volverse loco buscando como se hace en otros años(30).

3.               Sin embargo, de ser posible es mejor que la persona designe a un שליח, para hacer la Bedikah en su momento apropiado(31). Hay quienes dicen que es mejor hacerlo uno mismo antes de salir en lugar de hacer que alguien que no es miembro de la familia lo haga por uno(32).

4.              Si planea regresar antes de Pesach y tiene temor de que puede regresar en Erev Pesach y no le quedara tiempo para la Bedikah, hay que hacerla antes de irse o hacerla inmediatamente al regresar(33).

## ¿Dónde?
1. Solamente hay que inspeccionar las áreas en las que se acostumbra manejar Chametz(34).

2.        Sin en la casa hay niños pequeños, la Bedikah debe hacerse en todos los aposentos de la casa porque no estamos seguros de los lugares a los que los niños pudieron haberlo llevado (35).

3.        Hay que hacer la Bedikah en las áreas en las que se planea comer después de la Bedikah, en la noche y en la mañana; y luego volver a revisar después de haber comido y antes de destruir el Chametz(36).

4.        En un edificio de apartamentos hay que inspeccionar la escalera, los closets, etc; para todos, después de haber dicho la Brakhah en su propia casa (sin interrupciones que no sean relevantes a la Bedikah)(37).

5.        Hay costumbre de no hacer la Bedikah en el lugar destinado para almacenar el Chametz que se le venderá a un goy para Pesach(38).

6.        Si el pórtico de la casa está techado y cerrado, se considera como otra habitación y necesita ser inspeccionado e incluido en la Brakha(39).

### **Rentar la casa a un no Judío.**
1. Si se renta la casa con el Chametz que haya dentro a un no Judío para Pesach, quedara exento de la Bedikah, pero no es correcto hacer esto, más bien lo apropiado es rentar la casa a excepción de un aposento y realizar la Bedikah en ese lugar antes de Pesach sin pronunciar la Brakhah, antes de marcharse para Pesach(40).

-          El aposento que no se renta debe ser uno al que se lleve Chametz regularmente para poder realizar la Bedikah en él, de otro modo la obligación no existe en cuanto a la Bedika y no se conseguirá nada con dejar ese aposento sin rentar(41).

### **Inquilinos**
1. Si el propietario tiene las llaves al el momento que se debe hacer la Bedikah, el propietario está obligado a hacer la Bedikah(42).

2.        Si el inquilino la casa tiene la llave de la propiedad cuando llega la hora de la Bedikah (el catorce de Nisan en Tzeit HaKochavim) y se ha hecho una adquisición Halákhichah (se pagó la renta en efectivo), entonces él tiene que llevar a cabo la Bedikah(43)

3.        No obstante, si el inquilino tiene la llave de la casa mas no ha hecho una adquisición de acuerdo a la Halakhah, hay quienes dicen que el dueño debe llevar a cabo la Bedikah(44). Ciertamente el propietario o el inquilino pueden designar un שליח por medio del otro y cumplir con la Bedikah(45).

4.        Una persona que rente una casa para Pesach debe inspeccionar a la perfección las partes de la casa en las que colocara sus utensilios y los alimentos que se consumirán para Pesach. Deberá también inspeccionar el resto de la casa, sin embargo, areas privadas que no deben ser accedidas por los inquilinos - ya indicado explicita o implicitamente - no deberán ser inspeccionadas por los inquilinos(46).

### **Huéspedes en un Hotel**
1. Si se llega a un hotel antes del catorce de Nisán y planea quedarse ahí para Pesach, entonces hay que hacer la Bedikah en la habitación recitando la Brakha(47). Algunos dicen que deberia hacerse la inspección sin recitar la Brakhah(48).

-          Si la habitación está bien limpia, hay que traer Chametz antes de hacer la Bedikah(49).

2.        Si se llega al hotel el catorce de Nisan, si en el hotel ya se hizo la Bedikah el mismo catorce por la noche, no hace falta hacer la Bedikah de nuevo. No obstante, si el hotel no la hizo, debe de hacerse recitando antes la Brakhah(50).

3.        Si eres huésped del hotel únicamente para el catorce de Nisán y planea marcharse antes de Pesach, aun así debe hacer la Bedikah, pero sin recitar la Brakhah(51).

### **Estudiante de Ieshivah**
1. Si un estudiante de Ieshiva se marcha dentro los treinta días antes de Pesach, inclusive que no tenga la intención de regresar para Pesach, tiene la obligación de hacer la Bedikah la noche antes de marcharse sin decir una Brakha(52), pero deberá hacerla con una vela o con un foco(53), y luego decir Bitul(54).

2.        No debe sentarse a estudiar, trabajar o comer antes de haber hecho esta Bedikah, tal y como se hace la Bedikah el catorce de Nisan(55).

3.        Si un estudiante de Ieshiva permanece en la Ieshiva en Pesach, está obligado a llevar a cabo la Bedikah en su dormitorio; y si se hace la noche del catorce deberá hacerla con Brakha(56). No obstante, hay quienes sostienen que esta Bedika debe hacerse sin Brakha(57).

4.        Sin embargo, si la Ieshiva decide vender todos los dormitorios a un goy para Pesach, entonces no hay obligación de realizar la Bedikah(58).

### **Visitando a un Pariente para Pesach**
1. Si se queda con un pariente - o un amigo - para Pesach, y tiene un dormitorio en el que se quedara, debe participar en la Bedikah escuchando la Brakhah sobre esta y luego debe revisar el dormitorio en el que se quedará (59).

### **Colonia de Bungalows**
1. Quien se marcha de su bungalow dentro de los treinta días antes de Pesach deberá llevar a cabo la Bedikah antes de partir, sin embargo si se marcha más de treinta días antes no se debe hacer la Bedikah y es suficiente con realizar el Bitul Chametz sobre el Chametz que esté en la casa, a menos que tenga la intención de regresar a la casa para Pesach, en cuyo caso hay que hacer la Bedikah antes de Pesach(60).

### **Oficina**
1. Debe hacerse la Bedikah en la oficina (si es que se lleva comida allí), sin embargo, no debe hacerse en la noche antes de Pesach, sino en la noche en la que uno se marcha de la oficina y no volverá hasta después de Pesach(61).

### **Lugares que fueron inspeccionados antes de Pesach**
1. La casa debe limpiarse con anterioridad a que llegue Pesach, pero aun así debe realizarse la Bedikah (con Brakhah) la noche antes de Pesach(62).

2.        Si se limpió un gabinete, armario o closet sacando todo utensilio que estaba dentro y se revisó con una linterna de manera que se verificó que no quedo nada de Chametz en las esquinas y en las junturas de sus piezas, se considera como si ya ha sido inspeccionado y no hace falta hacer Bedikah en él (63). Sin embargo, si existen áreas que requieren una examinación detallada (como lugares que haga falta agacharse o revisar por debajo de algún mueble), debe hacerse la Bedikah en su momento indicado (64).

### **Hendiduras y grietas**
1. Hoy día, no hace falta revisar en las grietas y hendiduras en el piso porque nadie esconde o guarda Chametz en las pocas hendiduras o grietas en el piso(65).

2.        Si un trozo de algo que es Chametz es difícil de alcanzar, no hace falta volverse loco para quitarlo y con hacer Bitul es suficiente (66).

### **Libros**
1. Muchas autoridades sostienen que no hay una obligación real de inspeccionar Sefarim (libros) en busca de migajas de Chametz(67). Si se van a revisar, hay que hacerlo por adelantado y no debe esperarse hasta la noche del catorce de Nisan(68).

2.        Libros de Birkat Hamazon y panfletos con Zmiros que se usan el resto del año no deberían ser utilizados en Pesach, sino deben ser vendidos a un no Judío en la Mekhirat Chametz(69).

### **Bolsillos**
1. Hay que inspeccionar los bolsillos de las prendas en las que suele guardarse Chametz(70). Muchas autoridades permiten revisar estos bolsillos antes de la noche del catorce de Nisan(71).

2.        Si nunca se coloca Chametz en los bolsillos, hay quienes dicen que no es necesario inspeccionarlos, mientras que otros dicen que deben ser revisados, pues el Chametz puede haber llegado ahí de manera inadvertida(72).

### **Debajo de los Muebles**
1. Hay que inspeccionar debajo del refrigerador, la estufa, los sillones y cualquier mueble que pueda correrse (73).

### **Rentarle la Casa a un Goy**
1. Si no se va a estar en casa en Pesach y no va a rentarle la casa aun goy durante  esos días, no es apropiado no hacer la Bedikah(74).

### **La Oficina**
1. Hay quienes dicen que debe realizarse la Bedikah en el lugar de trabajo en la noche usando una vela(75). Por otro lado, que hay quienes dicen que no hace falta que se haga la noche del catorce sino el último día en el que uno está en la oficina antes de Pesach. Adicionalmente, no es necesario que se haga con una vela ni hay que colocar los diez trozos de Chametz como se hace en casa. Tampoco se dice una Brakhah por esta Bedikah(74).

### **Automóvil**
1. Es correcto inspeccionar el coche la noche del catorce haciendo uso de una linterna. De otro modo, debe inspeccionarse en la mañana. No hace falta decir una Brakhah cuando se inspecciona el coche(77). Esto aplica inclusive si es un coche que no será utilizado en Pesach(78).

2.        Compañías de autobuses o aerolíneas que son propiedad de Judíos deben inspeccionar sus unidades en cuanto al Chametz antes de Pesach(79).

3.        Si se inspeccionó el coche antes de la noche del catorce y está limpio, hay autoridades que dicen que no hace falta revisarlo nuevamente la noche de la Bedikah(80).

### **La Shul (sinagoga)**
1. El Gabai o cualquier otro individuo debe llevar a cabo la Bedikah en la Shul o en la Beit Midrash. Algunos dicen que debe hacerse la Brakhah por esta Bedikah(81), y hay quienes dicen que debe hacerse sin Brakhah(82), y lo mejor es que la persona diga la Brakhah por la Bedikah en su casa y que luego haga la Bedikah en Shul (sin hacer una interrupción irrelevante a la Bedikah)(83).

-          No se hace Bitul Chametz después de la Bedikah en la Shul o en la Beit Midrash(84) a menos que esta pertenezca a alguien, en cuyo caso es el propietario que debe realizar la Bedikah y hacer el Bitul Chametz(85).

## Comer o Laborar antes de la Bedikah
1. No se debe empezar a comer (más de un KaBeitzah de pan) o a hacer una labor empezando media hora antes de Tzeit HaKochavim hasta después de la Bedikah(86). Sin embargo, todavía se puede comer fruta media hora antes de Tzeit HaKochavim, pero no después de Tzeit HaKochavim(87).

2.        No se debe empezar a estudiar Torah a partir de Tzeit HaKochavim hasta después de que se haya hecho la Bedikah. Hay quienes agregan que no se puede empezar a estudiar Torah incluso media hora antes de Tzeit HaKochavim pero hay quienes lo permiten hasta Tzeit HaKochavim(88).

3.        Si ya se empezó a estudiar Torah, laborar o comer aun cuando es de día y continuó hasta la noche, de acuerdo a Sefardim no debe interrumpir para hacer la Bedikah, y de acuerdo a Ashkenazim hay que detener lo que sea que uno esté haciendo a partir de Tzeit HaKochavim para llevar a cabo la Bedikah(89).

4.        Inclusive quien hace la Bedikah en la noche antes de salir de viaje, no debe realizar ninguna actividad a partir del momento en que cae la noche(90).

## Vela
1. La inspección debe llevarse a cabo con una vela de cera con una mecha y no una antorcha (ni con dos velas juntas) (91).

2.        Si no se puede usar una vela, se puede usar una linterna (92). Aunque hay autoridades que aseguran que se puede cumplir la obligación con una linterna, lo tradicional y la regla impuesta por la costumbre es usar una vela(93).

3.        No hace falta apagar las luces eléctricas mientras se hace la Bedikah(94).

4.        Ver también Fuentes en Hebreo para el uso de una linterna en Bedikat Chametz

## Si no se hace la Bedikah
1. Si no se llevó a cabo la Bedikah durante la noche, deberá de hacerse durante el día antes de la sexta hora después de la salida del sol (hora Halákhica) y si se olvida hacerla antes de la sexta hora, debe hacerse durante todo el día de Erev Pesach con una Brakhah(95). SOLO SE PUEDE HACER BITUL CHAMETZ DESPUÉS DE LA BEDIKAH HASTA LA SEXTA HORA DESPUÉS DE LA SALIDA DEL SOL EN EREV PESACH(96).

2.        Si no se hace la Bedikah antes de Pesach, se deberá hacer en Pesach a menos que se haya hecho Bitul Chametz antes de Pesach, en cuyo caso se hace la Bedikah durante Chol HaMoed sin decir Brakhah(97).

3.        Si no se hace Bedikah durante Pesach, la deberá hacer después de Psach sin recitar la Brakhah(98).

4.        Cualquier Bedikah incluso se haga fuera de su tiempo apropiado, deberá hacerse con una vela(99).

## Si se halla Chametz
1. Si se halla Chametz en Iom Tov, no debe quemarse sino cubrirse con un utensilio para quemarlo después de Iom Tov(100). Hay quienes dicen que hoy día podemos pedirle a alguien no Judío que lo deseche en el sanitario(101).

2.        Si se halla Chametz en Chol HaMoed debe quemarse pero sin decir una Brakhah, inclusive si ya se hizo Bitul Chametz o se vendió el Chametz a un goy antes de Pesach(102).

3.        Hay quienes dicen que si se vendió el Chametz a un goy antes de Pesach y luego halla Chametz, debe guardarse con el Chametz que se le vendió al goy y no quemarlo(103).

## Costumbre al llevar a cabo la Bedika
1. Hoy día en que las casas se limpian de Chametz de antemano, es suficiente inspeccionar asegurándose que las áreas de la casa quedaron limpias; si no, deberá quitar el Chametz de ahí(104).

## Distribuir Diez Pedazos de Chametz
1. La costumbre es distribuir diez pedazos de Chametz para buscarlos mientras se hace la Bedikah(105). Hoy en día, ya que limpiamos nuestras casas de Chametz desde antes, hay quienes mantienen esta costumbre mientras que otros dicen que ya no hay obligación y que es solamente una costumbre(106).

2.        Estos trozos de Chametz deben ser duros para que no se desmoronen y deben ser colocados en lugares alejados de niños y ratones(107). Además, es aconsejable envolverlos para que no hagan migajas(108).

3.        Hay que ser muy cuidadoso de no perder ninguno de los trozos de Chametz(109).

## ¿Cuanto es Suficiente?
1. No hace falta volverse loco y perder la dulzura del carácter, si no deberá de buscar lo razonable para que pueda disfrutar del Seder(110). Es cuestión de sentido común y la búsqueda solo debería ser superficial (sin embargo no “demasiado” superficial)(111).

## ¿Qué hacer si se halla Chametz después de la Bedikah?
1. De hallarse Chametz después de la Bedikah, no hace falta inspeccionar la casa de nuevo(112).

## ¿Que pasa si se hace la Bedikah antes de la noche del catorce?
1. Si se hace la Bedikah a la luz de una vela el trece mientras aún es de día, debe hacerse la Bedikah la noche del catorce sin pronunciar la Brakhah(113).

2.        Si se hace la Bedikah a la luz de una vela la noche del trece, no debe hacerse la Bedikah el catorce por la noche solamente si fue lo suficientemente meticuloso de no traer más Chametz a la casa. Si desea hacer la Bedikah de nuevo el catorce la deberá hacer sin Brakhah(114).

Rama (432:2) cita una opinión que dice que la costumbre de colocar diez trozos de pan en la casa es para asegurarse que se halle Chametz para evitar que la Brakhah de Biur Chametz haya sido dicha en vano. Sin embargo, concluye el Rama, que no es necesario pues la intención en la Brakhah es destruir el Chametz que se halle. Ta”z (432:4) desaprueba esta costumbre porque se pueden perder los pedazos. Por otro lado, Rabí Iaakov Reischer en Chok Iaakov (432:13) defiende la costumbre y discute que colocar los trozos motiva a ser meticuloso en la búsqueda y no abandonar la labor a menos que el Chametz sea hallado por completo.

106)     Shaar HaTziyun 432:12 cita el Emek Halakha que sostiene que, ya que hoy día en las personas limpian sus casas de antemano, deben colocarse estos diez trozos de Chametz para la Brakhah de la Bedikah no sea Levatalá. Sin embargo, Halikhot Shlomo 5:12 discute que aun así se puede decir la Brakhah sin poner estos diez trozos, porque la Bedikah incluye la inspección de las áreas que no han sido aseadas apropiadamente, no obstante, la costumbre es hacerlo de esa manera.

107)     Mishna Brurah 432:12

108)     Halachos de Pesach (pg 80)

109)     Mishna Brurah 432:13

110)     Rav Schachter en OU Pre-Pesach Webcast 5771 entre los minutos 19:30 y 21.

111)     Rav Israel Belsky en OU Pre-Pesach Webcast 5771 entre los minutos 24 y 25. Ver Haggadah de los Roshei Ieshiva (pag 13) que registra la costumbre de Moshe de llevar a cabo la Bedikah en su pequeño departamento por más de una hora. Esta Bedikah no debe ser hecha como si no se hubiera limpiado del todo, pero se requiere de todos modos. Esta es la opinión del Sha’arei Teshuvah 433:2, Daat Torah 433:2, Chokhmat Shlomo 433:11, Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach citado en Mevakshei Torah Ohr Efrayim pág 532, Kinian Torah 2:122.

112)     Mishna Brurah 438:4, Halikhot Shlomo 5:22

113)     Mishna Brurah 433:1

# Bedikat Chametz

Source: Halachipedia: Bedikat Chametz

Link: [https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Bedikat_Chametz](https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Bedikat_Chametz)

Categories: `Holidays`, `Pesach`

Exported: 2025-12-30

## Texts for Bedikat Chametz
### Brachah
1. Before the bedikah one should make the berachah of "אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו על ביעור חמץ" - "Asher Kidishanu BeMitzvotav VeTzivanu Al Biur Chametz".¹ If one accidentally recited "על ביטול חמץ" - "Al Bitul Chametz," they have fulfilled their obligation.² One has also fulfilled their obligation if he recites "לבער חמץ" - "Livaer Chametz."³
2. One may not speak between the berachah and beginning the bedikah; if one indeed spoke regarding matters that were unrelated to the bedikah another berachah must be recited.⁴
3. Once the bedikah commences, it is preferable not to speak about unrelated matters until the bedikah has been completed; however, in this case another berachah would not be necessary. Additionally, once the bedikah begins one **may** speak about matters relating to the bedikah.⁵
4. If one didn’t make the bracha before beginning bedika one can make it as long as one hasn’t finished bedika. Nonetheless, if one has finished the bedika, one should make it without shem umalchut in the morning before burning the Chametz and some say that one may make it then with shem umalchut.⁶
5. One may make the bracha on the bedika with many people listening and then split up for each person to check an area in the house.⁷ If someone didn’t hear the bracha and it’s difficult to finish the bedika without that person’s help, he may help without making a Bracha.⁸
6. If one is checking two houses one may should make only one bracha and do bedika on both.⁹
7. There’s no shehecheyanu on the bedika.¹⁰
8. Some say that one should wash one’s hands before performing bedika.¹¹

### Bitul
1. After the bedika one should recite the following form of bitul chametz: "כל חמירא וחמיעא דאיכא ברשותי, דלא חזיתיה ודלא בערתיה, לבטיל ולהוי הפקר כעפרא דארעא" meaning "All chametz or leaven in my possession that I have not seen, and have not destroyed, shall be nullified and become ownerless, like the dust of the earth."¹² For more information, see the [Bitul Chametz](https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Bitul%20Chametz) page.

## When
1. One should perform bedikat chametz in the beginning of the night on the fourteenth of Nisan.¹³ Generally, one may not do it earlier by day or the night before.¹⁴
2. If one usually follows רבינו תם, some say that one should make sure to start the bedika after Tzet HaKochavim of רבינו תם.¹⁵ and some say that one should begin before Tzet HaKochavim of רבינו תם at the time of accepted Tzet HaKochavim (while it’s still slightly light outside).¹⁶
3. If one is praying with a minyan one should pray first and then perform bedika.¹⁷ However, if one is praying at home, preferably one should appoint someone else to do bedika while one prays, otherwise, pray first, unless one usually prays at home in which case some say one should check first and some say one should pray first.¹⁸ Some recommend for a person davening at home that they should daven maariv at the ideal time, which is Tzet Hakochavim, and then starting the bedika.¹⁹
4. If one is going to come home after Tzet HaKochavim one should appoint someone as an agent (Shaliach) so that it can be done at the proper time. However, if the man is working at night and wants to fulfill the mitzvah himself, he may appoint his wife to do bedika (with a Bracha) on the whole house except for one room and then do bedika (with a Bracha) in that room when he returns.²⁰
5. If a person did bedikat Chametz on the 13th at night he doesn't need to redo the bedikat on the 14th at night, though the institution was to check on the 14th at night specifically.²¹ Some say that one doesn't need to do bedika again but one should do at least one room again.²²
6. An area with three walls and is very open to sunlight should be checked on the 14th at night and after the fact can be checked during the day without a candle since there is a lot of sunlight there.²³

## What
1. Some poskim say that one must search even for crumbs of Chametz and remove them.²⁴ However, most poskim say that there's no obligation to check for crumbs of chametz, but the places where one will have kosher for pesach food must be cleaned of all crumbs of chametz so that not even a crumb gets into the food which will be eaten on Pesach.²⁵
2. Chametz that is buried in the cracks in the floor or between the back of a cabinet and the wall and people can’t reach one doesn’t have to do bedika there.²⁶

## Cleaning the House Beforehand
1. Thirty days before Pesach a person should begin to be cognizant of the fact that he will need to clean and remove all chametz in his house. Therefore, he should not leave chametz in any place that will be difficult to remove later.²⁷
2. One should sweep (or vacuum) the house before the bedika in order to clean it well.²⁸
3. The minhag is to clean the house well and remove all the chametz from around the house before the bedika, and then do a cursory check of the house without checking every crack or crevice.²⁹ The same applies if the house was cleaned and washed well by non-Jews.³⁰
4. In rooms that you eat chametz you should check under the beds and cabinets, however, in rooms that you don’t eat chametz it is sufficient to sweep under the beds and cabinets without checking there carefully.³¹

## Who
1. One who is sick must appoint a שליח to do bedika in his place.³²
2. One who is an Onen, one who is in the first day of mourning, must appoint a שליח (agent) to do bedika in his place.³³

## Bedika before Leaving for Pesach
1. If a person leaves one’s house more than 30 days before Pesach and doesn’t plan to return for Pesach one doesn’t have to do bedika.³⁴ Nonetheless one must do Bitul when the times comes wherever one is.³⁵
2. If a person leaves one’s house within 30 days of Pesach and doesn’t plan to return for Pesach one must do bedika with a candle the night before one leaves and then do Bitul Chametz afterwards, however, the bedika is done without a Bracha.³⁶ Even if one plans on returning before Pesach one should do bedika before leaving in case one gets delayed until right before Pesach when it is too late to do bedika upon returning.³⁷This only applies if one left for a long trip but if one left for a short trip then there's no concern that one will be delayed. The determination of what is a long trip or short trip all depends on the circumstances. The most factor is whether one left oneself enough time to return home to do bedika even in the event of a delay.³⁸
3. However, if possible it’s preferable to appoint a שליח to do Beidika for oneself at the proper time.³⁹ Some say that it’s better to do it oneself before going rather than have a non-family member (such as a neighbor) do it for oneself.⁴⁰
4. If one plans on returning before Pesach if there’s a fear one will return on Erev Pesach without time for bedika one should do it before going, otherwise do it when one returns.⁴¹
### Early Bedika
1. If one is not going to be home for Pesach it is sufficient to do a proper bedika according to the law by just looking for the Chametz (though not just a superficial look) and one doesn’t have to drive oneself crazy like one does every year.⁴²
2. When doing bedika before the night of the fourteenth one should still scatter the pieces of chametz before bedika. Some say one shouldn't scatter the pieces when doing bedika early.⁴³
3. When doing bedika early a person should sweep or vacuum like he would normally would for bedika.⁴⁴
4. The night before he leaves he should do bedika and it is forbidden to do melacha or eat before bedika just like bedika on the night of the 14th.⁴⁵

### Personal Obligation to Do Bedika
1. If a Jew was living or renting a non-Jew's house and was there until within 30 days of Pesach and then left for the duration of Pesach, there is a discussion whether he is obligated in bedikat Chametz in the house he was staying at before leaving. Sephardim hold that if he is going to fulfill bedikat chametz in another house he isn't obligated to do bedikat chametz in the house that he is leaving since it is a non-Jew's house. However, if he isn't going to fulfill bedikat chametz someone else then he should do it in the house he is leaving since bedikat chametz is secondarily a personal obligation. Of course, bedikat chametz is an obligation upon a house that a Jew lived in where he ate chametz but it is also a personal obligation to take care of in some location.⁴⁶ However, according to Ashkenazim there is no personal obligation of bedikat chametz. Therefore, in this case since he moved out of the house and left it to a non-Jew before Pesach he was exempt from bedikat chametz in that house.⁴⁷ Some say that he it is only exempt if the non-Jew moved in before Pesach.⁴⁸
2. If a Jew was living or renting a Jew's house and left it within 30 days of Pesach, the owner of the house is obligated in bedikat chametz.⁴⁹ If the owner is not religious and won't do bedikat chametz a person should do bedikat chametz before he leaves the house.⁵⁰

## Where?
1. One only has to check in area where one would have brought Chametz.⁵¹
2. If one has small children one must do bedika in all rooms in the house because one doesn’t know where Chametz was brought.⁵²
3. One should do bedika on the area where one plans to eat after the bedika for that night and the next morning and then one should check that area again in the morning.⁵³
4. In an apartment building one person should check the stairwell, closets, etc. for everyone after having made a Bracha for bedika in his own house (without making interruptions that aren’t relevant to the bedika).⁵⁴
5. The minhag is not to do bedika in the areas where one stores Chametz and is going to sell to a goy for Pesach.⁵⁵
6. If one's porch is roofed and fenced in, it is considered like any other room that needs to be checked with a bracha.⁵⁶

### Renting One's House to a Non-Jew
1. If one is renting out one’s house and the Chametz in it to a non-Jew for Pesach one will have exempted oneself from bedika but it’s not proper to do so, rather it’s correct to rent one’s house except for one room and do bedika without a Bracha in that room before one leaves for Pesach.⁵⁷
    1. The room which one leaves not rented in order to bedika should be a room which one usually brings Chametz otherwise there’ll be no obligation of bedika and one will have accomplished nothing by leaving that room not rented.⁵⁸

### Renters
1. If the owner/landlord has the keys at the time of the bedika, then the owner is obligated in bedika.⁵⁹
2. If the renter has the key to the house at the time of bedika (14th at Tzet HaKochavim) and he has made a halachic acquisition (paying with cash), then he’s obligated to do bedika.⁶⁰
3. However, if the renter has the key to the house but didn’t do a halachic acquisition, many say that the owner is obligated and some say that the renter is obligated.⁶¹ Certainly the owner or renter can be appointed a שליח by the other and fulfill the obligation of bedika.⁶²
4. A person who rents a house for Pesach, the areas which one will put one’s food utensils and actual food should be checked perfectly well. The rest of the house should be checked well, however, the areas which are private areas and the renters are not supposed to open (explicitly mentioned or implicitly understood) the renters do not have to bedika on those areas.⁶³
5. If someone rented a house for Pesach and it was stipulated that the owner did bedikat Chametz beforehand and it is revealed that it isn't the case, nonetheless, the renter must do the bedikat Chametz. Some say that the owner must pay the renter the cost of doing the bedikat Chametz on his behalf.⁶⁴ It isn't an option for the renter to blame the owner for not having done bedikat Chametz and live there anyway, he needs to do it himself.⁶⁵
6. If someone rents a house from a Jew after the night of the fourteenth one can assume that it had bedikat Chametz.⁶⁶

### Hotel Guests
1. If one arrives in the hotel before the 14th at night and plans on staying Pesach, then one should perform bedika in the room with a Bracha.⁶⁷ Some maintain that one should check without a Bracha.⁶⁸
    1. If the room is cleaned well one should bring Chametz into the room before doing bedika.⁶⁹
2. If one arrives in the hotel on the day of the 14th, if the hotel did a bedika on the 14th at night one doesn’t need to do bedika, however, if the hotel didn’t do bedika, one should do so with a Bracha.⁷⁰
3. If one is a guest in the hotel only for the 14th and plans on leaving before Pesach one should still do bedika but without a Bracha.⁷¹

### Yeshiva Student
1. If a Yeshiva student is leaving his dorm or apartment within 30 days of Pesach, even if he isn’t returning on Pesach, he has an obligation to do bedikat Chametz the night before he leaves, without a Bracha⁷², but with a candle or flashlight⁷³, and then do Bitul.⁷⁴
2. One shouldn’t eat, work, or learn prior to performing this bedika, just like one who performs bedika on the 14th.⁷⁵
3. If a student in Yeshiva is in Yeshiva on Pesach, he is obligated to perform bedika in his dorm room and if it’s done on the 14th at night it should be done with a Bracha.⁷⁶ However, some hold that the bedika should be made without a Bracha.⁷⁷
4. However, if the Yeshiva decides to sell all the rooms to a goy for Pesach, then there’s no obligation to perform bedika.⁷⁸

### Going to a Relative for Pesach
1. If one is staying at a relative for Pesach and has a room where will one be staying one should participate in the bedika by listening to the Bracha on the bedika and then checking the room one will be staying in.⁷⁹

### Bungalow Colony
1. If one leaves one’s bungalow colony house within 30 days of Pesach one has to bedika before one leaves, however if one leaves longer than 30 days before Pesach one doesn’t have to bedika and it’s sufficient to do Bitul Chametz on the Chametz in that house unless one is going to come to the house on Pesach in which case one has to bedika before Pesach.⁸⁰

### Areas which were Cleaned before Pesach
1. One has to clean the house before Pesach and still do bedika (with a Bracha) the night before Pesach.⁸¹
2. If one cleaned a closet completely by removing every single vessel, checked using an electric light and there no small confined areas or hidden places in the closet then it’s considered checked and doesn’t require bedika.⁸² However, if there are areas which require close examination (like getting down on one’s hands and knees) one should still do bedika at the appropriate time.⁸³

### Cracks
1. Nowadays, one doesn’t have to check in the cracks in the floor because no one actually hides Chametz in the few and small cracks in the floor.⁸⁴
2. If a piece of Chametz is too difficult to reach one doesn’t have to go crazy in order to remove that Chametz (and Bitul is sufficient).⁸⁵

### Books
1. Many authorities maintain that there is no obligation to check sefarim for Chametz crumbs.⁸⁶ If one is going to check one may do so in advance and doesn’t have to wait until the night of the 14th.⁸⁷
2. Benchers and Zemiros booklets of the rest of the year should not be used on Pesach but rather sold to a non-Jew with Mechirat Chametz.⁸⁸

### Pockets
1. One should check the pockets of clothing in which one sometimes puts Chametz.⁸⁹ Many permit checking the pockets before the night of the 14th.⁹⁰
2. If one never put Chametz in the pocket, some say that one doesn’t have to check but others hold that one must check because Chametz may have been placed there inadvertently.⁹¹

### Under Furniture
1. A person should check under the refrigerator, stove, couches, and all movable furniture.⁹² Some say that one doesn't need to move a heavy oven or furniture which isn't regularly moved to get chametz behind or to the side of it if one's hand can't reach it as is. He can rely upon bitul chametz.⁹³
2. A crack or crevice very low to the ground, within 3 tefachim, doesn't need to be checked since a person doesn't usually use that area.⁹⁴ If a person has children he does need to check since they could easily put chametz there.⁹⁵

### On Top Of Furniture
1. A person should check on top of the furniture, ovens, and cabinets unless they have a slanted roof which would make it abnormal to store things there.⁹⁶

### Inside Machines
1. Chametz which is stuck inside of a machine, for example a mixer, and can't be accessed unless dissembled by a professional doesn't need to be removed.⁹⁷

### Roof
1. If a person uses his roof he needs to do bedikat chametz there. If it is a slanted roof and he doesn't use it it wouldn't require bedikat chametz.⁹⁸

### Renting or Selling the House to a Non-Jew
See [Selling Chametz](https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Selling%20Chametz) for the main topic of selling chametz.

1. If someone rents their house and sells the chametz in it to a non-Jew for Pesach, if he sells it on the 14th (standard sale of chametz) some say he isn't obligated to do bedikat chametz, while others hold he is obligated since it wasn't sold at the time of bedika.
2. If he rents his house and sell the chametz in it on the 13th (early sale), he is certainly exempt from doing bedikat chametz.⁹⁹
3. Some say that one should specifically rent the rooms and not sell them in order that the rooms not become exempt in mezuzah over Pesach and then after Pesach the mezuzah's are invalid since they were exempt and then left up.¹⁰⁰
4. Some poskim question if it is proper to use these leniencies to exempt oneself from bedikat chametz altogether without a reason.¹⁰¹

### Office
1. One should do bedika in the place where one works. Some say that this should be at night using a candle after one does bedika at home relying on the bracha that one made for one's home.¹⁰² Others say that that it doesn’t have to be done on the night of the 14th rather one should do it the last day one is there before the 14th of Nissan. Additionally, it doesn’t have to be done with a candle nor does one have to put out pieces of Chametz. No bracha is made on this bedika.¹⁰³

### Car
1. It’s proper to check one’s car(s) for Chametz on the night of the 14th using a flashlight. Otherwise, one should check it during the day. No Bracha is required for performing bedika in a car.¹⁰⁴ This is true even of a car that will not be used on Pesach itself.¹⁰⁵ Some say that one can check the car with a flashlight by day even initially.¹⁰⁶
2. Public bus companies or airplane companies that are Jewish must check for Chametz before Pesach.¹⁰⁷
3. If one checked the car and it is clean before the night of the 14th some say that it doesn't need to be checked the night of the 14th.¹⁰⁸

### The Shul
1. A gabbai or other appointed individual should perform bedika in the Shul or Bet Midrash. Some say that one should make a Bracha on this bedika¹⁰⁹, and some say that one shouldn’t make a Bracha¹¹⁰ and it’s preferable to have the one doing the bedika to make a Bracha for bedika of his home and then do bedika in the Shul (without making an interruption not relevant to the bedika).¹¹¹
    1. One doesn’t have to do Bitul Chametz after bedika of the Shul or Bet Midrash¹¹² unless it belongs to an individual in which case one should do Bitul Chametz.¹¹³

## Eating or Working before bedika
1. A person shouldn’t start a job or start eating (a KeBeitzah of bread) from a half hour before Tzet HaKochavim, until one has done bedika.¹¹⁴ However, one may continue to eat fruit a half hour before Tzet HaKochavim, but not after Tzet HaKochavim.¹¹⁵
2. A person shouldn’t start learning from Tzet HaKochavim until one has done bedika. Some add that one may not learn from a half hour before Tzet HaKochavim and some permit until Tzet HaKochavim.¹¹⁶
3. If one began to learn, work, or eat during the day and continued into the night, according to Sephardim one doesn’t have to stop to do bedika, and according to Ashkenazim one must stop at Tzet HaKochavim in order to perform bedika.¹¹⁷
4. Even someone who is doing bedika the night before he leaves shouldn't eat or do activities beforehand after nightfall.¹¹⁸

## Candle
1. One should check using a single wax candle and not a torch (or even two candles together).¹¹⁹
2. If one is unable to use a candle, one should use a flashlight.¹²⁰ Some say that one can fulfill the obligation with a flashlight, but the minhag is to use a candle or to begin with a candle.¹²¹ One should recite a bracha when doing bedikat chametz with a flashlight.¹²²
3. One doesn’t have to turn off the electric lights while performing the bedika. Furtherfore, some say that specifically one should turn on the lights because one can check better with the lights on.¹²³
4. See also Hebrew sources for using a flashlight for bedikat Chametz

## If One Didn’t Do Bedika
1. If one didn’t do bedika at night one should do so during the day before the sixth hour (halachic hours) and if one forgot to do it before the sixth hour one should still do it on Erev Pesach with a Bracha.¹²⁴ One can only do Bitul Chametz after the bedika until the sixth hour of Erev Pesach.¹²⁵
2. If one didn’t do it before Pesach, do it on Pesach unless one did Bitul Chametz before Pesach in which case one shouldn’t do bedika on Pesach with a Bracha.¹²⁶
3. If one didn’t do bedika during Pesach, do it after Pesach without a Bracha.¹²⁷
4. Any bedika not at the appropriate time should be done with a candle.¹²⁸

## If One Finds Chametz
1. If one finds Chametz on Yom Tov one shouldn’t burn it but rather cover it and then burn it after Yom Tov.¹²⁹ some say that nowadays one should have a non-Jew flush it down the toilet.¹³⁰
2. If one finds Chametz on Chol HaMoed one should burn it but not make a Bracha if one either did Bitul Chametz or selling of Chametz to a non-Jew before Pesach.¹³¹
3. Some say that if one sold one’s Chametz before Pesach and then one finds Chametz on Pesach, one should store it away with the other Chametz that’s sold to the non-Jew and not burn it.¹³²

## Performing a Cursory Bedika
1. Nowadays, when people clean the house of Chametz in advance, it’s enough to quickly double check to see if that area was cleaned from Chametz and if it wasn’t to remove the Chametz.¹³³ However, others disagree and hold that even if one cleaned the house well it is necessary to do a serious and thorough bedika. One is strict will be blessed.¹³⁴
2. A person doesn’t have to make themselves crazy, one just to be reasonable not to overwork oneself so that one can enjoy the Seder.¹³⁵ It’s a judgment call and one should do a peripheral check (not too peripheral).¹³⁶
3. Even if a person works really hard to check every crevice of the house for chametz, as is necessary in a house with little kids, he should know that according to his effort he is rewarded.¹³⁷

## Scattering Ten Pieces of Chametz
1. The minhag is to scatter ten¹³⁸ pieces of Chametz to be found during the bedika.¹³⁹
2. Nowadays, when people clean the house of Chametz in advance, some poskim maintain that it is an absolute obligation to put out pieces of chametz, while others hold it is still just a minhag.¹⁴⁰
3. These pieces should be hard Chametz that doesn’t cause crumbs and it should be placed in an area that’s protected from children or mice.¹⁴¹ Additionally, it may be advisable to wrap it so that it doesn’t make crumbs.¹⁴²
4. One should be careful not to lose any of the pieces.¹⁴³Therefore, it is a wise practice to write down where the pieces were hidden so that they're not accidentally forgotten.¹⁴⁴
5. Each of the pieces of chametz should be less than a kezayit so that in case one is lost there will be no question that bitul chametz suffices to nullify it.¹⁴⁵
6. The minhag is that some family member hides the pieces and someone else finds them. If he is doing bedika by himself he should nonetheless hide the pieces and find them himself.¹⁴⁶

## If one found Chametz after the Bedika
1. If one found Chametz after the bedika one doesn’t have to recheck the house.¹⁴⁷

## If one did bedika before the night of the 14th
1. If one did bedika during the day of the 13th to the light of a candle one should do bedika the night of the 14th without a Bracha.¹⁴⁸
2. If one did bedika during the night of the 13th to the light of a candle, one doesn’t have to do bedika on the 14th at night if one was careful not to bring Chametz there and if one wants to do bedika it should be done without a Bracha.¹⁴⁹

¹: Tur and Shulchan Aruch O.C. 432:1, Kitzur Shulchan Aruch 111:7. Mishna Brurah 432:3 and Chazon Ovadia Part 1 page 44 explain that we don't recite al bedikat chametz because the search is only for the purpose of the destruction.

²: Mishna Brurah 432:3

¹³: Shulchan Arukh O.C. 431:1. Mishna Brurah (431:1) writes that according to the Shulchan Arukh one should check after tzeit ha-kochavim. Raavad in Katuv Sham on Rif Pesachim 2a writes that the language of the Mishna *אור* implies that bedika should be done while there is light outside in the beginning of the night. Ran 1a quotes this Raavad and explains it should be done at the beginning of the night so you don't delay and become lazy about it or forget. However, The Gr”a (431:1) cites the Raavad as holding that it should be done while there is light outside because that is more accurate than saying it should be done at night. See Maaseh Rav (#178) who says that the Gra would begin Bedika slightly before Tzet HaKochavim. Nonetheless, Rabbi Eliyahu Spira in Eliyah Rabbah (431:5) explains that even the Raavad agrees that one shouldn’t begin until tzeit ha-kochavim, however, at that time there still is a little bit of light outside.

However, the Ramban (Milchamot 4a) argues that there's an insistence on night in the Gemara since a candle is more effective at night than the day. He proves this from the Yerushalmi Pesachim 1:1 as well. Raavad (Katuv Sham 4a), Ran 1b, Ritva 4a, and Maharam Chalavah 4a all accept the position of the Ramban and reject the Baal Hameor. Furthermore, the Maharam Chalavah Pesachim 4a s.v. amar writes that one may not do bedika on the night of the thirteenth since one may not do a complete job since it isn't the time for the mitzvah and then one will rely on that incomplete bedika.

²³: Gemara Pesachim 8a establishes that a house with three walls that is exposed to the sunlight can be checked to the sunlight. Bach 433:2 organizes three approaches in the rishonim: 1) Rashi 8a, Rif 4a, Smag Asin 39, and Smak 98 hold that even initially it is permitted to check the area exposed to the sunlight during the day. 2) Rambam Chametz Umatza 2:4 holds that initially one should check the night of the 14th and after the fact one should check during the day. 3) Rabbenu Yerucham 5:1 38c holds that one may not check the area on the 13th by day but even initially one can check it during the day of the 14th. He concludes that initially it may not be checked during the day. This is also the opinion of the Taz 433:2, Magen Avraham 433:3, Biur Hagra 433:2, Chok Yaakov 433:3, and Mishna Brurah 433:5.

²⁴: [Chazon Ish OC 116:18](https://www.hebrewbooks.org/pdfpager.aspx?req=14336&pgnum=348) writes that you need to section off chametz crumbs like chametz of a non-Jew (Pesachim 6a). See regarding checking sefarim that the Chazon Ish checked his sefarim for crumbs. See, however, Gemara Pesachim 6b that implies that crumbs aren't significant and don't need bedika. Maharam Chalavah 6b s.v. may maintains that one doesn't need to destroy a crumb less than a kezayit except for dough pieces which could combine into a kezayit. This also seems evident from Piskei Rid 6b and Rosh Pesachim 1:9. Magen Avraham 432:5 also implies that crumbs don't need bedika.

²⁵: Pesachim 6b implies that crumbs are unimportant and don't need to be checked for. [Rabbi Eliezer Melamed in Peninei Halacha](http://ph.yhb.org.il/category/%D7%A4%D7%A1%D7%97/04-%D7%91%D7%93%D7%99%D7%A7%D7%AA-%D7%97%D7%9E%D7%A5/) says that the halacha is that one doesn't have to check for crumbs of chametz but in the areas where one will have kosher pesach food one must remove all crumbs of chametz. He brings the Shaar HaTziyun 442:60 as his proof. Yabia Omer OC 7:43, Or Letzion 1:32, and Halichot Shlomo ch. 5 fnt. 10 agree.
    
    * For more details see Yabia Omer 7:43 who quotes many sources on the matter. Rashi Pesachim 45a s.v. mklal writes that it isn't necessary to destroy chametz that is less than a kezayit and one doesn't violate Baal Yiraeh on less than a kezayit. (It isn't clear if this assumption changes on a biblical level throughout the discussion of the gemara.) Ri Mlunil Pesachim 45a s.v. amar, Talmidei Harashba 45a, Trumat Hadeshen (Pesakim 164), Shulchan Aruch O.C. 442:11, and Magen Avraham 442:10 in understanding Shulchan Aruch all agree with this opinion. The Taz 442:5 wonders why it isn't necessary to destroy chametz less than a kezayit, even though there is no Baal Yiraeh because of the concern that one will come to eat it. Bigdei Shesh 442 explains that even though eating chametz that is less than a kezayit is biblically forbidden it isn't karet and therefore, it isn't necessary to remove. Peni Yehoshua 45a s.v. mishna and Magen Haelef 442:11 agree. This is also the opinion of the Meiri 45b s.v. shni, Maharam Chalavah Pesachim 6b s.v. may, Shulchan Gavoha 442:22, and Pri Chadash 442:8 that one doesn't have to remove chametz less than a kezayit unless it is like dough that could stick together. Maharil (Drashot Afiyat Matzot), Magen Avraham 460:2, Shiurei Knesset Hagedola, Eliya Rabba, Graz, Pri Chadash, Zera Emet 1:48, and Mateh Moshe 579 there agree. Riaz (Pesachim ch. 2 2:2) quotes his grandfather the Rid who says that crumbs which do not stick do not need to be removed, however, the Riaz disagrees and thinks that there's no distinction between dough and crumbs and everything needs to be removed. Also, Magen Avraham 442:10 quotes poskim who are strict with owning less than a kezayit, though the Magen Haelef 442:10 argues. Yabia Omer rules like the Meiri, Rid, and Maharam Chalavah as well as the many achronim who think it isn't necessary to remove or destroy crumbs. See however, the Maharam Chalavah 45a s.v. amar and Rabbenu Dovid 6b s.v. iylayma who explicitly state that there is a biblical violation of baal yiraeh on less than a kezayit. Maharam Chalavah 45b explains that even though there is baal yiraeh on less than a kezayit there is no reason to remove crumbs on the floor since they get dirty.
    * Rabbi Akiva Eiger 1:218 likes the suggestion of the questioner that even though there is no baal yiraeh on less than a kezayit there is a mitzvah of tashbitu. Shagat Aryeh 81 holds that there’s no baal yiraeh on less than a kezayit and proves it from Pesachim 29b and Beitzah 7b. He answers the Taz's question by explaining that eating less than a kezayit of something prohibition is forbidden because it could combine with more forbidden food and become forbidden retroactively. Owning chametz less than a kezayit at a time would only be forbidden once one has the full kezayit and not retroactively.

³⁵: *Rashi Pesachim 6a s.v. afilu holds that it is unnecessary even to do bitul if one is leaving prior to 30 days. He doesn't explain why there is no problem of Baal Yiraeh owning chametz on Pesach. The Bach 436:1 answers that chametz left out for 30 days will be destroyed by dicentrgrating, putrifying, or being eaten by rodents or bugs. Thus, it is possible on a Torah level not to be concerned for the chametz if it was left in the house for 30 days.[Baal Haitur (Biur Chametz p. 120a)](https://www.hebrewbooks.org/pdfpager.aspx?req=20516&st=&pgnum=254) seems to explain that Rashi is lenient because it is like chametz that a wall fell upon. Even though it is true that even if a wall collapses upon chametz bitul is still necessary (Gemara Pesachim 31b) that is only rabbinic and might not apply in this case (see Bach). See Petach Dvir (fnt. 80 to Baal Haitur) who rejects that understanding of the Baal Haitur.
    * The Tosfot Harosh Pesachim 6a s.v. iy, Chidushei Haran Pesachim 6a, Ran on Rif 2b s.v. garsinan dispute Rashi and all hold that it is necessary to do bitul even when you leave before 30 days and are exempt from bedika. The Bet Yosef 436:1 quotes the Ran without any dispute and Rama 436:1 codifies it as the halacha. The Gra 436:4 clarifies that it indeed a biblical problem if one doesn't do bitul. Sephardim also agree with this Rama as the Kaf HaChayim on Shulchan Arukh Orach Chayim 436:12:1 writes.

Rashi Pesachim 6a s.v. dayto implies that only if one intended to return in the middle of pesach is it necessary to do bedika before leaving, otherwise one could do beidka upon returning. Ran Pesachim 2b s.v. chemso spells this out and notes the disagreement with the Rambam. He supports Rashi's reading based on the Yerushalmi.

Similarly, the Chok Yakov 436:18 thinks that the Rama's language isn't precise and it is equally true that the Jew is exempt if the non-Jew was allowed in but didn't move in. He answers that the second Jew is a *shaliach* (trans. agent, Hebrew: שליח) of the first Jew.

⁶⁴: Gemara Pesachim 4b, Shulchan Aruch and Rama Orach Chaim 437:3. The Gemara establishes that even if the owner lied that he did Bedikat Chametz on the house, the renter can't renege on the deal since a person would want to do the mitzvah of Bedikat Chametz himself or by paying someone else to do it. 
    
    * Tosfot 4b s.v. hamaskir writes that we're discussing a rental that began prior to the 14th of Nissan in which case it is reasonable that the renter has to do Bedikat Chametz, otherwise it would be obvious that there is an obligation upon the owner to do it.
    * The Ran Pesachim 1b s.v. hamaskir learns that it is discussing a rental that happened on the fourteenth on the assumption that Bedikat Chametz was done and one can't retract because people like to do mitzvot themselves or pay for them. Maharam Chalavah 4b s.v. iybaya agrees.
    * The Ramban takes it a step further and says that even if it was stipulated explicitly that they did Bedikat Chametz it isn't a void sale since people like to do mitzvot themselves or pay for them. However, the Ramban says that people would only like to do the mitzvah themselves or pay for it if they are later going to be paid back. Certainly the owner should have done the Bedikat Chametz and if he is around the renter can force him to do it but if it isn't possible then it isn't a voided deal. This approach of the Ramban is cited by the Rabbenu Dovid 4b vharav, Maggid Mishna (Chametz Umatza 2:18), Ritva Pesachim 4b s.v. hamaskir, Ran Pesachim 1b s.v. hamaskir, and Meiri 4b s.v. hamaskir. The Rama 437:3 quotes the opinion of the Ramban.

⁶⁵: Ran Pesachim 1b s.v. hamaskir clarifies that even though the responsibility of the Bedikat Chametz was upon the owner the night of the fourteenth but if he neglected or intentionally didn't do it, the renter may not live there without Bedika. He explains that even with a non-Jew's chametz in one's house one needs to section it off with a wall of ten tefachim. This implies that it is necessary to find and remove the chametz in the house even though it isn't one's chametz.

⁶⁶: Gemara Pesachim 4a, Rosh Pesachim 1:2, Rambam Chametz Umatzah 2:17, Rabbenu Dovid 4b s.v. iybaya and Maharam Chalavah 4b s.v. ule'inyan in explaining the opinion of the Rif 1b, Shulchan Aruch Orach Chaim 437:2. However, the Talmid Harashba 4b s.v. garsinan thinks that we hold that we assume that the house wasn't checked.

⁶⁷: Chovat Hadar (end of Sefer Dinei Bedikat Chametz), Siddur Pesach KeHilchato 12:8, Chag HaMatzot (Halachot VeMinhagim 5:32), Otzar Halachot vol 2 pg 124, Piskei Teshuvot 437:1. Rav Hershel Schachter on [OU Pre-Pesach Webcast 5771](https://oukosher.org/passover/webcast/pre-pesach/ou-kosher-pre-pesach-webcast-5771-2011/) between minutes 4:30 and 5:30 explains that even though the room is cleaned by the cleaning staff before one gets there that doesn't mean it is sufficiently checked so that there's no chametz in there on Pesach. Rabbi Aryeh Lebowitz in [Ten Minute Halacha - Bedikas Chameitz when Staying in a Hotel](http://www.yutorah.org/lectures/lecture.cfm/856001/rabbi-aryeh-lebowitz/ten-minute-halacha-bedikas-chameitz-when-staying-in-a-hotel/) agrees. Also, Rav Schachter added that in order to recite a bracha one should bring in some chametz such as a cookies before the time of the bedika.

⁷²: The Gemara Pesachim 6a says that one who leaves his house within 30 days of Pesach, should do Biur even if he doesn’t plan on being home during Pesach. Rambam (Chametz 2:16) explains that this includes doing Bedika. Shulchan Aruch 436:1 agrees. Mishna Brurah 436:6 writes that one should do Bedika with a candle the night before leaving. Rama 436:1 writes that there’s no Bracha for this Bedika since it’s not performed on the night of the 14th. Torat HaYeshiva 14:2 applies this halacha to a Yeshiva student in dorms.

⁷³: Halachos of Pesach (p. 86) quotes Rav Moshe saying that a flashlight is better than using a candle and Rav Aharon Kotler as saying it is equivalent to a candle. Halichot Shlomo 5:11 writes that if one can’t use a candle, one should use a flashlight. Chazon Ovadyah (p. 38) and the Debrecener (cited by A Guide to Practical Halacha v. 5 p. 41 n. 5) agree.

Kaf HaChaim 436:7 and Nitei Gavriel 28:4 agree. Kovetz MeBet Levi (Nissan 5761 pg 85) writes that this also applies to a Yeshiva Student doing Bedika in his dorm the night before he leaves. # Bedikot after Marriage

Source: Halachipedia: Bedikot after Marriage

Link: [https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Bedikot_after_Marriage](https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Bedikot_after_Marriage)

Categories: `Niddah`

Exported: 2025-12-30

## Bedikot after Marriage
1. A woman who has a veset may not be strict to do a bedika before or after tashmish.¹ However, when not in front of her husband and not at the time of tashmish the more the woman checks the better.²
2. A woman without a veset according to many authorities should check herself before and after tashmish the first three times. However, many authorities argue that no checks should be done at all. A couple should consult their rabbi as to the proper practice.³
3. Many poskim hold that these bedikot only need to be an external check, while some say that they need to be a thorough bedika.⁴
4. It is permitted to do a check in the crevices of the vagina after tashmish and there is no concern of hashchatat zera because that zera isn't going to cause a pregnancy anyway. He proves it from the fact that when taharot existed a woman would have to do bedikot after tashmish in the crevices of the vagina and chazal didn't say it was a problem of hashchatat zera.⁵

## Renewed Concern of Seeing during Tashmish
1. If a woman once saw blood after tashmish even if it wasn’t immediately afterwards she should be concerned to check before and after tashmish. If she has a veset she only needs to check once but if she doesn’t have a veset she needs to check three times.⁶
## Who is Exempt
1. A pregnant woman doesn’t need to do checks before or after tashmish.⁷
2. A woman who knows that her period is at least a certain number of days she doesn’t need to perform any bedikot before or after tashmish within that interval. For example, if she doesn’t see her period before 25 days, she doesn’t need bedikot before then.⁸
## When the 3 Bedikot Do Not Count
1. If she did bedikot within the interval of days that she knows her period doesn't come prior to, (such as if her period is never less than 25 days) they don’t count towards the three bedikot that are necessary.⁹
2. These three bedikot don’t count towards her count if they were done when she was pregnant.¹⁰

## References

¹: In Niddah 12a, Rav Yehuda said that a woman should not be strict to do a bedika before tashmish since that will cause her husband to become agitated and will prevent them from having tashmish. Additionally, Rav Huna said a woman should not do a bedika after tashmish again because that will cause her husband to come agitated and will prevent having tashmish again. Accordingly, the Rama 184:1 rules a woman who has a veset may not be strict to do a bedika before or after tashmish. Shulchan Aruch 186:1 writes that a woman with a veset may not do a bedika before tashmish in front of her husband.

²: Taharat Habayit v. 1 p. 143

³:
    * The Mishna Niddah 11a writes that a woman should check herself for blood before tashmish. Shmuel in the gemara 11b holds that it is only an obligation for someone who deals with taharot (ritually pure foods and vessels) otherwise there’s no obligation to check before tashmish. This applies whether or not she has a veset. 
    * The gemara Niddah 12a also quotes Shmuel as saying that a woman doesn’t need checks to be pure to her husband. However, in the gemara Niddah 12b Shmuel is quoting as holding like Rabbi Chanina Ben Antiganus who required checks for a woman without a veset. The gemara is unsure if he requires checks for every women or just if a woman deals with taharot. Rashi (s.v. maan) understands the conclusion of the gemara as saying that there’s no contradiction between the statements of Shmuel and Rabbi Chanina only requires checks if a woman was dealing with taharot. However, the Rabbenu Chananel (cited by Rosh 1:5) understands the gemara as saying that there’s a contradiction between those who quoted Shmuel. Thus, he holds that a woman without a veset requires checks before and after tashmish. This is also the opinion of the Rambam (Isurei Biyah 4:16) and Rosh (Niddah 1:5). Rabbenu Tam (Sefer Hayashar no. 174) learns the gemara like Rabbenu Chananel but doesn’t necessary agree as to the halacha. However, Tosfot (12b s.v. dematni), Sefer Hatrumah (no. 94), Smag (Lavin no. 111), and Roke’ach (317 s.v. bedika) hold like Rashi. 
    * Furthermore, the Rif (Ketubot 60b) rules that even according to Rabbi Chanina, who we follow even for a woman who isn’t dealing with taharot, a woman only needs checks 3 times after tashmish both for her and her husband. According to the Ramban (Milchamot Ketubot 60b) and Bet Yosef 186:1 the Rif thinks that she would also need a bedika before tashmish those 3 times. If those 3 times are clean she is permitted to her husband without any more bedikot. If she sees blood all three times she is forbidden to her husband. This is also the opinion of the Ramban (Hilchot Niddah 6:1) and Rashba (Torat Habayit 7a). 
    * The Shulchan Aruch and Rama YD 186:1 hold like the Rif and not the Rambam or Rashi. However, the Shach 186:1 argues that we should follow the opinion of Rashi that no checks are necessary. Rabbi Mordechai Willig (Niddah Shiur 66 and notes to The Laws and Concepts of Niddah by Rabbi Zvi Sobolofsky pg. 315) holds like the Shach. The Laws of Niddah v. 1 p. 281 and Rav Ovadia in Taharat Habayit v. 1 p. 146 holds like Shulchan Aruch, even though he cites the Zivchei Tzedek 186:2 who wrote that the minhag of Baghdad was like the Shach. Shoshanat Ha'amakim 7:5 writes that you should check in accordance with the opinion of Chacham Ovadia

⁴: Chavot Daat 186:1 holds that an external check is sufficient, while the Shulchan Aruch Harav 186:6 holds that a real bedika is necessary. The Laws of Niddah v. 1 p. 281 holds like the Shulchan Aruch Harav and the Taharat Habayit v. 1 p. 147 like the Chavot Daat. Igrot Moshe YD 2:75 agrees with the Chavot Daat.

⁵: Igrot Moshe YD 2:75

⁶: The Chavot Daat 186:2 explains that seeing once even not right after tashmish that is enough to make her concerned to check afterwards, once if she has a veset, and three times if she doesn't.

⁷: Pitchei Teshuva 186:4 citing the Maharam Paduah 25 writes that a pregnant woman doesn’t need to check before or after tashmish since she’s not supposed to see her period. Shiurei Shevet Halevi 186:2:2 considers being lenient even within the first 3 months of pregnancy.

⁸: Trumat Hadeshen 247, Shulchan Aruch YD 186:3 unlike the Chavot Daat 186:3

⁹: Chatom Sofer on S”A YD 186:2, Shiurei Shevet Halevi 186:2:4

# Before the Bracha

Source: Halachipedia: Before the Bracha

Link: [https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Before_the_Bracha](https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Before_the_Bracha)

Categories: `Brachot`

Exported: 2025-12-30

## Physical preparations of one's body
1. When reciting a bracha, one's mouth should be empty so that one can fully praise Hashem.¹
2. One must wear a Kippah while making a Bracha.² If one doesn't have a Kippah one should cover your head with your hand and a little bit of your sleeve or ask a friend to cover your head with his hand (even without a sleeve).³
3. One should be dressed properly before making any bracha especially Birkat HaMazon⁴
4. One should figure out which bracha one has to make before one begins to say the bracha so that one can have the proper intent when one says Hashem's name.⁵
5. One should be careful to make brachot with kavana (the proper intent) thinking about blessing with hashem's name, who granted us great kindness in allow one the fruit or bread one has or that he commanded one to perform a mitzvah that we are about to perform. Thus, a person should make the bracha slowly and loud out in order to inspire the requisite kavana.⁶
6. One should not recite a bracha if one needs to go to the bathroom.⁷ Some say that it is permitted if one can hold it in for 72 minutes⁸ and others say it is forbidden.⁹
7. Making brachot in front of an ervah has the same halacha as learning Torah. See [Laws_of_Learning_Torah](https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Laws%20of%20Learning%20Torah#learning-in-front-of-ervah).
8. Making brachot in an unclean place has the same halacha as learning Torah. See [Laws_of_Learning_Torah](https://halachipedia.com/index.php?title=Laws%20of%20Learning%20Torah#learning-in-an-unclean-place).

## Preparation of the food
1. One should only make the Bracha only after one has the food available and present so that the Bracha can take effect on something. Therefore, one should open the packaging of the food prior to the Bracha.¹⁰
2. One should hold the food that one is making the bracha upon.¹¹ After the fact, one doesn't need to repeat the bracha.¹²
3. One who drinks from a water-fountain, ideally, should have the water in a cup prior to the Bracha, however if that’s not possible, one should let the water run from the faucet momentarily prior to making the Bracha. If that last option isn’t possible or one is concerned about wasting water, he may make the Bracha on the water even before letting it run.¹³
4. One should prepare the food before making a bracha; for example, one should break open a nut or peel a fruit in order to eat it right after the Bracha.¹⁴
5. However, one shouldn't cut a large or whole piece of food before the bracha; for example, one shouldn't cut a fruit, or a piece of meat before the bracha, rather make the bracha and then cut it.¹⁵

## References

¹: Gemara Brachot 50b writes that if one forgot and put food into one's mouth, if the food isn't something that's easily ruined it should be spit out. On this the gemara explains that one should spit it out so that one could have his entire mouth involved in praising Hashem based on the pasuk ימלא פי תהלתך (Tehillim 71:8). The Shulchan Aruch 172:2 rules like this gemara and the Kitzur Shulchan Aruch 6:2, Mishna Brurah 172:7, Kaf HaChaim 172:4, and Vezot HaBracha (p. 7) concur.

²: Shulchan Aruch 91:3

³: Shulchan Aruch 91:4 writes that using one's hand to cover one's head isn't sufficient for a head-covering, but a friend covering one's head would be sufficient. Mishna Brurah 91:10 adds that it is considered a head-covering if one uses one's hand along with a bit of the sleeve.

⁴: Shulchan Aruch 74:4 writes that one should cover one's lower body (with pants) even if one's upper body is revealed prior to saying Shema. Yet, Mishan Brurah 74:22 writes clearly that this is only for extenuating circumstances, otherwise one should always dress properly even for regular brachot and all the more so for Shema. VZot HaBracha (pg 8) quotes Rav Elyashiv that one should dress properly for brachot even by the beach. Or Letzion 13:3 and VeTen Bracha (pg 212) in name of Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach say that one must wear proper clothing for Birkat HaMazon just like the requirement of Ituf (see Shulchan Aruch 183:5)

⁵: Kitzur Shulchan Aruch 6:1

⁶: Kitzur Shulchan Aruch 6:1 quoting the Sefer Chasidim

⁷: Rama 92:1

⁸: Mishna Brurah 92:7

⁹: Shaarei Teshuva 6:5

¹¹: Shulchan Aruch 167:3 writes that one should hold the bread while reciting Hamotzei. Mishna Brurah 167:22 explains that the reason for this is that one should make the bracha immediately before performing a mitzvah and not too far in advance.

¹²: Mishna Brurah 167:22 based on Shulchan Aruch 206:5

¹³: Vezot haBracha (Chapter 1, pg 8) based on Mishna Brurah 206:19 who writes that ideally one should have water in a cup so that the food is present during the Bracha. However, if that’s impossible, Rav chaim Pinchas Sheinburg (quoted by Vezot HaBracha) suggests letting the water run prior to the Bracha so that it’s evident what one is making a Bracha on. Lastly, if that’s impossible, one may make the Bracha even while the faucet is closed.

¹⁴: Mishna Brurah 206:19 writes that one should prepare food before the bracha so that it's ready to eat right after the bracha. Vezot HaBracha (Chapter 1) gives the examples of removing the shells a nut and peeling a fruit.

¹⁵: Vezot HaBracha (end of Chapter 1) based on Aruch HaShulchan 202:11, and Vezot HaBracha quotes the example of leaving a piece of meat in its full state from Rav Elyashiv and Rav Mordechai Eliyahu.
